title: SaturnAI — POC scoping: latency & throughput SLOs (TTFT vs TPOT)
summary: POC scoping call to define latency and throughput SLOs for an intent-classification / chat assistant use case. Discussed TTFT vs TPOT, p95/p99 targets, measurement plan (synthetic + production shadowing), workload sizing and timeline for a 2-week pilot with benchmark suite and automated harness.
topics: p95 / p99 latency targets and tail behavior
workload sizing: QPS, seq length distributions, concurrency
benchmark plan: synthetic load, shadow traffic, tooling
SLO measurement and alerting: sampling, tagging, and trace hooks
transcript:
16:00 - Maya (Redwood AE): Hey everyone thanks for joining, we'll keep this to about 45 minutes. quick intro round?
16:01 - Alex (SaturnAI - CTO): Hi, Alex here, we've got Priya and Samir as well. we're trying to scope a POC to validate latency SLOs for our customer chat assistant.
16:02 - Maya: Great, high level what are the success criteria you need from the POC?
16:03 - Priya (ML Eng): We want to prove we can meet p95 120ms TTFT and p99 300ms TTFT on our typical prompt distribution, and also measure TPOT so we know per-token cost impact when responses are longer.
16:03 - Derek (Redwood SE): Cool, just to align on terms — when you say TTFT you mean time from request -> first token from the model, yes? And TPOT is average per-token generation time after first token.
16:04 - Priya: Exactly, TTFT is what our UX team cares about, TPOT matters for throughput/cost.
16:05 - Samir (Infra): Our current infra is GKE with VMs backed by A100s for heavy jobs. we'd prefer to benchmark both hosted and a private deployment variant — mostly concerned about predictable tail latency under bursty traffic.
16:06 - Maya: That makes sense. For the POC we usually do a 2-week run: week 1 baseline benchmarking with your modeled traffic and synthetic spikes, week 2 tuning (batching, quantization, routing) and shadowing live traffic. Does that timeline work?
16:06 - Nora (Product): Sounds good, do you have a standard benchmark harness or scripts?
16:07 - Derek: Yes, we have a benchmark harness that can replay traces and also do synthetic QPS/seq_len distributions. We'll push a lightweight runner you can run on your infra or we can run against our hosted infra.
16:08 - Alex: Important: we need to measure p95/p99 for both TTFT and end-to-end response time for multi-turn. Also want percentiles under 95th and 99th with 95% confidence, and request sampling for traces.
16:09 - Derek: We'll emit per-request traces, token counts, and bucket by model variant. Note transcription can be imperfect but we'll ensure metrics include seq_len, tokens_out, and scheduling latency.
16:10 - Priya: What about measuring TPOT — do you instrument token emission times or use aggregate?
16:11 - Derek: We capture time between first-token and final token, and compute per-token rate. We also measure steady-state TPOT (token/s) and also cold-start contributions. TPOT is typically influenced by batching and KV cache hits.
16:12 - Samir: Our case has a lot of short prompts (avg 12 tokens) but some long ones up to 512. How do you recommend configuring batching?
16:13 - Derek: For mixed distributions we suggest dynamic batching with a short max wait (5-15ms) for TTFT-sensitive routes. For endpoints tolerant of slightly higher TTFT you can increase micro-batch sizes to improve TPOT. We'll try a few configs during week 2.
16:14 - Maya: On SLO numbers, you proposed p95 120ms TTFT and p99 300ms TTFT — are those hard constraints or targets?
16:15 - Alex: They're our aspiration. If we can show p95 <120 and p99 <350 that's acceptable for now but we'd like to understand failure modes where p99 jumps.
16:15 - Derek: We'll record percentiles and also provide histograms with tags for region, model variant, and cold vs warm cache. We'll also add a synthetic spike test to catch queueing issues.
16:17 - Priya: About measurements: we want both synthetic benchmarks and production shadowing. Shadowing will let us see real distribution and micro-bursts. How do you handle privacy/PII in shadows?
16:18 - Maya: We can hash or redact payloads; in Private deployments data never leaves your VPC. For hosted we'll follow retention config and can sign an addendum for hashed logs. We also support KMS and HSM for key management.
16:19 - Samir: Security ok. For hosted, can you expose audit logs and per-token billing traces?
16:20 - Derek: Yes — token-level cost breakdown and trace IDs per request. We'll include a link to our security pack in the follow-up.
16:20 - Alex: Great. Benchmarks: what exact scenarios will you run?
16:21 - Derek: Our recommended suite: (1) baseline steady-state at 20 QPS with seq distribution mimic (70% short, 25% medium, 5% long), (2) burst tests ramp to 200 QPS for 60s, (3) tail-pressure test with concurrent large-seq requests, (4) multi-turn chat session sim with 5-10 turn conversations to measure cumulative latency. We'll capture TTFT, TPOT, tokens_out, kernel queuing, and GPU utilization.
16:22 - Priya: For success criteria we want p95 TTFT <120ms and p99 <350ms for baseline load, and TPOT steady-state <3ms/token for medium sequences. Also want max tail latency under burst to remain under 1s for 99.9%?
16:23 - Derek: 99.9 is aggressive for burst; we can aim to show behavior and propose mitigations (dedicated capacity, autoscale, fallback model variants). We'll demo fallback routing and a cheaper model variant if latency spikes.
16:24 - Maya: Can you share your traffic patterns and QPS expectations?
16:25 - Alex: We expect 20-30 sustained QPS per region initially, peaks to 150-200 during promotions. Multi-region is in scope but for the POC we'll focus on us-west and eu-west.
16:26 - Derek: For measurement we'll need a replay trace and a small dataset of representative prompts. Please include percent of long sequences so we can tune KV cache and kernel selection.
16:27 - Priya: We'll prepare the trace. How do we validate p-values and confidence?
16:28 - Derek: We'll run each test 3 times, collect percentiles and compute confidence intervals; we'll also include bootstrap resampling in the harness. That will give you p95/p99 with error bounds.
16:29 - Samir: Any infra requirements for Private deployment?
16:30 - Maya: For Private we provide an on-prem package that runs in your k8s cluster with helm charts. Minimum is 4 GPUs for a small pool, but for realistic tail behavior we recommend at least 8 GPUs for the POC. We'll document resource profiles.
16:31 - Alex: Cost? we'll need a ballpark for dedicated vs hosted during the POC.
16:32 - Maya: We'll send a simple cost spreadsheet: token-based hosted estimate and a reserved-cost estimate for private/dedicated for the pilot period.
16:33 - Nora: What are the deliverables at the end of the 2 weeks?
16:34 - Derek: Deliverables: (1) Benchmark report with p50/p95/p99 for TTFT and TPOT; (2) tuning recommendations (batching, quant, routing); (3) a replayable benchmark artifact and config files; (4) go/no-go recommendation and next-step pricing.
16:36 - Alex: Good. Let's talk measurement specifics — sampling rates and telemetry retention.
16:36 - Derek: We'll sample 100% during controlled synthetic runs, and for production shadowing we recommend 10% sampling for full traces to limit overhead but 100% of aggregated metrics. Retention for raw traces depends on tier but we can deliver CSV/zip of POC traces.
16:37 - Priya: For TPOT we need per-token timestamps — is that heavy on bandwidth?
16:38 - Derek: Slightly; we can compress and sample. Also we can do server-side aggregation to compute mean token interval without sending every token time.
16:39 - Samir: Timeline and next steps?
16:40 - Maya: Action plan: You send replay traces and target SLO doc by Friday. We'll spin up hosted benchmarks in 48 hours and share runner for your private cluster. Week 1 run synthetic + baseline. Week 2 tuning and shadowing. End of week 2 we present results and recommendations.
16:41 - Alex: Sounds good. Any blockers?
16:41 - Priya: Need quantization notes — will quantization affect hallucination / quality? We need to include eval sets.
16:42 - Derek: We'll run quality regressions on a holdout eval set. Quantization profiles will be provided and we'll measure response quality with anchor prompts.
16:44 - Maya: Ok recap: deliverables and timeline as Derek said; we'll send security pack, benchmark runner, and cost spreadsheet. Next call to review results scheduled tentatively two weeks from today.
16:45 - Alex: Thanks all.
16:46 - (call ends)

Note: transcription has some minor ASR artifacts and occasional speaker label mismatches. Metrics names: TTFT, TPOT, p95, p99, p999 mentioned throughout.
